headline: Sweden's parliament will vote on Magdalena Andersson as prime minister on Thursday
deck: Andersson, the Social Democrats' leader, would govern with her party alone; she says no government parliament would tolerate can yet be formed.
standard: The Riksdag, Sweden's parliament, will vote at 12:00 on Thursday on whether Magdalena Andersson, leader of the Social Democrats, should be prime minister of a government of her party alone. Andreas Norlén, the Riksdag's speaker, announced the vote on Tuesday.

Andersson had told him that morning that talks had made progress but that no government the Riksdag would tolerate could yet be formed. If she falls short on Thursday, Norlén will call the other party leaders and speed up the process.
The four red-green parties won 176 seats in the election on 13 September, the centre-right bloc 173.
short: The Riksdag, Sweden's parliament, will vote at 12:00 on Thursday on whether Magdalena Andersson, leader of the Social Democrats, should be prime minister of a government of her party alone. She has concluded no government talks with other parties.
